source.publication: TIR 95-9: Income Taxation of Contributory Public Employee Pensions of Other States (Massachusetts DOR, 01/10/1996)
source.section: Statute quoted at the start ('any income from a contributory annuity, pension, endowment or retirement fund of any other state'); 2025 Form 1 Instructions PDF p22-23 Schedule Y Line 13 ('contributory pension income'); Form 1 lines 2a, 2c, 4, 10-22

worked: Federal AGI = New York noncontributory public pension 20,000.00 (person 0) + private pension 20,000.00 (person 0) = 40,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - 17,750.00 standard deduction (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 or older) = 22,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 20,000.00 New York noncontributory public pension (taxed: not from a contributory fund, so outside M.G.L. c. 62 s. 3(B)(a)(4) and TIR 95-9) + 20,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 40,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 40,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 40,000.00 - 0.00 = 40,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (single) = 4,400.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 1 x 700.00 = 700.00; line 2g = line 18 = 5,100.00. Line 19 = 40,000.00 - 5,100.00 = 34,900.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 34,900.00. Line 22 = 34,900.00 x 0.05 = 1,745.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 1,745.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 40,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 1,745.00.
